claim_reviews.rationale: 1843 pp. 677–678 describe the engine and operation/variable cards; the 1878 committee section IV records only a partial mill built. Scope is a design and mechanical computing.

The catalogue dates Sketch 13 to 1837 and identifies a punched-card mechanism; image shows multiple dates and a perforated arrangement. This is the archive date for a multilayer drawing, not proof of the exact date when each component was added or priority over earlier designs. Existing caveat expresses multiple stages.

1843 publication and reuse explanation are supported, but cited Note C p. 706 describes the proposed reversing prism specifically in a loom; for the engine prism itself cite Note E p. 720 (PDF p. 55). Correct the event evidence locator and supports so the loom proposal is not represented as an engine detail in Note C.

Direction from Jacquard weaving to Engine is directly attributed by Babbage in 1839 and Menabrea in 1843; p. 678 describes operation and variable cards, while the committee independently inspected design evidence. Yet Menabrea learned from Babbage and the 1879 source quotes him, and the sketch independently establishes a card mechanism but not its provenance. The required independent informative corroboration of consequential adaptation is not established by these citations. Obtain and cite an independent informative historical source for provenance, not merely a restatement deriving from the same testimony, or retain the relation as a candidate and mark origin unknown. Also remove to_event pointing to 1837 unless an original source ties the specific adaptation and later-described two-card functions to that drawing/date.
